anchors.paper_title: Working memory processes and intrinsic motivation: An EEG study
anchors.reason: Study paper reports the Sternberg task EEG (N=48) by the same authors, matching the dataset's task and participants; DataCite IsSupplementTo relation supports it.

metadata.methods_description: Participants performed a Sternberg task during EEG recording. Each trial had a 500-1000 ms fixation cross, then 1500 ms encoding, 2000 ms retention, and 1500 ms retrieval (probe letter). Participants answered yes or no with arrow keys. There were 200 trials in total, 40 per set size, in random block order with equal numbers of positive and negative probes. Stimuli were presented with Psychopy2. Triggers mark only stimulus onset, so retention and retrieval onsets must be computed from the trial design (1500 ms and 3500 ms after the trigger).

citation_details.title: Dynamic calibration of self-efficacy to cognitive load: the longitudinal mediation effect of state anxiety
citation_details.author: Xiaolong Li, Mu Xia
citation_details.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous research has shown that higher self-efficacy predicts lower cognitive load. Nevertheless, there is limited research exploring the dynamic calibration phenomenon of cognitive resources by self-efficacy during task execution through experimental methods. METHODS: This study elucidates the relationships and longitudinal mediating effects among self-efficacy, state anxiety, and cognitive load through two studies that employed convenience sampling. Study 1, which aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical understanding of the research question, is an interview study that examines the prevalence of fluctuations in self-efficacy among 22 university students through an in-depth interview. On the other hand, study 2 reveals further causal relationships through experimental methods. citation_details.title: Factors influencing self-regulated learning ability among Medical undergraduates in China: a cross-sectional study
citation_details.author: Jinmeng Huang, Chunxia Huang, Jian Qin, Kaiyong Huang
citation_details.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-regulated learning (SRL) is the core purpose of lifelong learning and the precondition for medical staff to continuously adapt to and excel in their current and future positions. Good SRL abilities positively impact the academic performance and clinical skills of medical students. Despite its importance, the factors influencing SRL among medical students in China remain under-explored. This study investigates these factors among Chinese medical undergraduates. METHODS: This cross-sectional survey was conducted among a convenience sample of undergraduate students at all four medical universities in Guangxi, using a questionnaire developed and tailored by Zude Zhu. Responses from 2,179 Chinese medical undergraduate students were included in the analyses. citation_details.author: Jianzhong Xu, Yuan Tian, Jintao Lu
citation_details.abstract: Purpose Driven by global sustainable development goals, this study addresses a gap in understanding the core motivation of Executive social responsibility (ESR) for enterprise Green innovation (GI), which has been overlooked in prior institutional and resource-based view studies. In addition, the present research explores the insufficiently investigated interaction between ESR and external stakeholders' pressure. citation_details.title: A Psychophysiological Investigation of Boredom Profiles Differing in Meaning, Stimulation and Subsequent Activity Choices
citation_details.author: Konrad Rudnicki, Koen Rummens, Heidi Vandebosch, Jolien De Schepper, Karolien Poels
citation_details.abstract: This study investigated the psychophysiological markers of distinct boredom profiles, defined along the meaning and stimulation dimensions of the Meaning and Attention Components (MAC) model. Psychophysiological markers were also assessed during regulatory activity choices following boredom to investigate their actual regulatory potential. The study ( N = 60, M age = 21.4, SD = 3.38, male = 35%) employed a mixed-factorial design, with meaning as a between-subjects factor and stimulation level as a within-subjects factor in a boring task. Electrodermal activity (EDA), as well as alpha and theta EEG frequencies, were recorded both during the task and during the subsequent activity choices (i.e., switching or adapting the boring task).
